finding.claim: deleteAccount calls canDelete() but discards the boolean result, so no authorization is enforced. Any caller can delete any account by id (broken access control / IDOR). The sibling closeAccount correctly uses assertCanDelete.
finding.source: Authenticated (any) user calling DELETE /accounts/{id} with an arbitrary account id

trace.note: deleteAccount(User u, long id) entry; id is attacker-controlled path param
account looked up by attacker-supplied id with no ownership check
canDelete(u, a) returns boolean that is ignored; no exception thrown on false

finding.guards_checked: canDelete (lines 9-11) would enforce admin-or-owner, but its result is unused. assertCanDelete is not called in this path. No other auth layer is present in the repo (single file). Also note: a missing id yields a null Account, causing NPE at line 22 (ownerId deref) for non-admins, which is only a minor robustness issue.

verdict.guard_found: canDelete (src/AccountService.java:9-11) returns a boolean (admin-or-owner) but its result is discarded at line 22. assertCanDelete (13-17) would throw but is only used in closeAccount (line 29). No other guard exists in the repo.
verdict.reason: At src/AccountService.java:22 `canDelete(u, a);` is a bare statement that ignores the boolean, so `accounts.remove(id)` at line 23 runs for any authenticated user; the only guard is the unused canDelete, and a non-admin caller with a nonexistent id gets an NPE at line 10, so the delete is not blocked for existing accounts.
